title: The quantum Navier--Stokes programme: from categorical regularity to the Clay problem
html:
The global regularity theorem and the regularity breakdown conjecture reframe the Clay Millennium Problem as a degeneration problem within a one-parameter family of well-posed equations.

The quantum reformulation. In a QOU with substrate parameter q > 1, the q-deformed Navier--Stokes system is globally regular. The classical problem is the limiting case q \to 1. We ask whether the family converges to a smooth solution of the classical Navier--Stokes equation, or develops singularities in the limit.

Significance of the categorical formulation. The mechanisms ensuring regularity for q > 1 are consequences of the categorical structure. The classical problem is hard because all mechanisms fail simultaneously at q = 1.

The research programme: five open problems.

Problem 1. Rigorous well-posedness proof. Complete the proof sketch. Establish that the q-Laplacian has compact resolvent with eigenvalues growing exponentially.

Problem 2. Rate of blowup. Determine the critical exponent \alpha such that the enstrophy growth rate scales as (q - 1)^{-\alpha}.

Problem 3. Identify the blowup mechanism. The singular set geometry at q = 1 may be a vortex sheet, a vortex filament, or a point blowup. The Berry phase structure constrains which blowup geometries are topologically allowed.

Problem 4. Universality of the critical point. Determine if the critical exponent depends on the initial data or only on the categorical structure. Analogy with statistical mechanics suggests universality.

Problem 5. Counter-example construction. Use the q \to 1 limit to construct an explicit counter-example to classical regularity. Track the maximum enstrophy for initial data that maximises the growth rate. The formation of an acoustic horizon provides a diagnostic for blowup.

Summary. The classical Navier--Stokes problem asks whether regularity survives the q \to 1 degeneration. The categorical mechanisms fail at q = 1. The 3d Navier--Stokes blowup is a structural consequence of the degeneration of the categorical contact structure. The physical universe lies in the regular regime; the millennium problem concerns a limit that the physical substrate does not attain.
